checks.name: Loads with the CSP, an empty-state message and no console errors
Typing a title and pressing Enter (real key events) adds a task and keeps focus in the field
Empty and whitespace-only titles are not added
Tags are lower-cased and de-duplicated; tasks sort by due date with undated last
Overdue incomplete tasks are highlighted; completed or future ones are not
Status filters (All / Incomplete / Completed) show the right tasks
Tag filter works, combines with the status filter, and shows "No matching tasks."
Task text and tags containing HTML are shown as text and never executed
Tasks and their done state survive a real page reload
Records saved by older versions and malformed records still render and can be deleted
A repeating task without a due date is rejected with a message and not saved
Completing a daily task 3 days overdue keeps it as history and adds tomorrow
Un-ticking a completed recurring task undoes it (no second open copy); re-ticking spawns again
A fast double click (tick then un-tick) leaves exactly one open copy
Weekly next date counts from the old due date, not from the day it was completed
Monthly repeats keep the 31st: Jan 31, then end of Feb, then Mar 31
A due year with five or six digits cannot freeze the page
Date logic: validDue, nextDue and stepDue return the hand-computed values
Every control has an accessible name and each task control names its task
Keyboard focus stays on the same row after Space toggles a task, and moves to a neighbour after Delete
At 375px wide (phone) nothing scrolls sideways or is clipped, even with very long text
A failed save shows a message, keeps what was typed, and the message clears after the next success
Text and controls meet WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1) in both light and dark colour schemes
New tasks default to Medium, the Priority dropdown returns to Medium after adding, and each task shows its priority
Tasks saved without a priority, and malformed priorities or repeats (including arrays), count as Medium and as not repeating
The list is ordered by due date, then priority (High first), with undated tasks last ordered by priority
The priority filter works alone and together with the status and tag filters, with the empty state
The next occurrence of a recurring task inherits its priority
Editing every field (title, due date, repeat, priority, tags) saves, closes the form, restores focus, and persists across a reload
Keyboard editing: Enter saves, Escape cancels, and focus returns to the Edit button (real key events)
Edit validation: an empty title, a repeat without a due date and an impossible date are rejected, nothing is saved and the draft stays
An edit in progress keeps its unsaved text when the list re-renders, and other Edit buttons are disabled meanwhile
Changing the due date of a monthly task starts a new series: the next occurrence uses the new day of month
Un-ticking never deletes a next occurrence the user has edited
Saving an edit does not overwrite a change made elsewhere meanwhile (no stale save)
Completing a repeating task on the last supported date (9999-12-31) ends the series without freezing the page
Saving an edit changes only the fields the user changed: another tab's change to a different field survives
Save and Cancel do nothing once the edit they belong to is closed: no error, nothing saved
Saving an edit to a task that was deleted elsewhere says so instead of looking successful
The task being edited stays visible when a filter would hide it, and keyboard focus never falls to the page body when the list empties
Records with a malformed nextId or anchorDay can still be ticked and un-ticked without errors
The footer is empty with no tasks (a "0 open · 0 done" would be wrong), then shows open and done counts that follow adding, ticking, un-ticking and deleting
The footer counts every task whatever the status, tag and priority filters show, and stays right when a filter shows nothing
Recurring tasks: ticking keeps open the same and adds a done, un-ticking undoes it, and editing changes nothing
Malformed records count as open, and a failed read clears the footer instead of leaving stale numbers
The footer sits below the list, is a polite live region that is never hidden (even when empty), and hides its separator dot from screen readers
A stored record whose title cannot be converted to text (such as {toString: 5}) no longer stops the list from loading
An unchanged count is not rewritten, so filtering or opening an edit does not make a screen reader announce the same numbers again
The only network requests are for the local page itself
Search filters by title and tag as you type: case-insensitive, trimmed, literal (no regex), empty search shows everything, no match shows the empty state
Search combines with the status, tag and priority filters, keeps the due-date order, and clearing it leaves the other filters in place
The search text is not saved: after a reload the box is empty and every task shows
The task being edited stays visible when the search would hide it, and the footer counts every task whatever is searched
Stored records with missing or odd titles and tags do not break the search
A list read that is overtaken by a newer render never overwrites it (typing while a task is added)
